findings.expected: OD-6: genuine misread with object and difficulty unchanged costs one A/B mark; no MR only where the object/difficulty changes (e.g. easier, no solution).
findings.actual: The design rules that any misread leaving P off the curve is a changed-object/no-solution case. Because C=q(q+a) is printed, misreading a, C or q always puts P off the curve; only k (exponent) misreads keep P on it (27/27). So a natural misread such as 3e^{2x}y read as 2e^{2x}y scores 3/5 (canonical) instead of 4/5 (MR-1), and in the show part only target-neutral C misreads remain MR-eligible.
findings.evidence: Own computation: (3,2,-4) with a misread 3->2 gives m=-8/3, P not on 2e^{2x}y+y^2=4; design 3/5 vs MR reading 4/5. Literal reading of OD-6 "leaves no solution" supports the design; comparable Cambridge practice would usually apply MR-1 here.
findings.repair: Judgement call at the margin, disclosed. Optionally state in the OWNER-CHECKPOINT OD-6 row that point-off-curve misreads are treated as changed-object, so Vitalis sees that OD-6 rarely applies to coefficient misreads in this recipe.

findings.expected: One deterministic OD-6 outcome per response.
findings.actual: Two edges are not settled. (i) C misread in (a) only (proof otherwise perfect; C differentiates to 0): the target guard makes it eligible (deduct S2 -> 3/4, total 8/9), but the :146 point-off-curve exclusion makes it ordinary marking (4/4, 9/9). (ii) An a/k misread in (a) that is target-ineligible, then carried into (b)/(c) via "using your derivative": canonical throughout gives 5/9; treating (b) as a fresh eligible first use gives 6/9. The :140 sentence "If an eligible new datum first affects only the normal part, N3 is its only possible deduction" describes only a misread of P, which :146 makes ineligible; the marks coincide (2/3) only if N2 DM is judged as usual on the misread point.
findings.repair: Add E/F fixtures fixing (i) and (ii); state that ineligibility of a datum persists across later parts, and that N2 is judged as usual on a misread point.

findings.locator: calculus-design.json misread_policy.deduction.selection ("Earliest earned A/B criterion ..."); criteria S4 "all preceding proofwork correct and complete", G5 "from a correct differentiated relation"
findings.expected: An MR deduction is a ledger adjustment that does not un-satisfy dependencies of later criteria.
findings.actual: The earliest earned A/B is often a slot other criteria depend on (G2 before G5; S2 before S4). The worked samples assume no cascade (G2 deducted, G5 kept: 4/5), but no criterion text says that a deducted award still counts as satisfied evidence for dependencies. A literal implementation could cascade to 3/5 or 2/4.
findings.evidence: WO :144 sample 4/5; JSON G5 qualifier "canonical gradient from a correct differentiated relation"; S4 qualifier "all preceding proofwork correct and complete".
findings.repair: State in the shared ledger rule that dependencies are tested on evidence before deduction; add a fixture (gradient-only k misread: 4/5, not 3/5).

findings.actual: Every worked/oracle stationary misread changes only the constant term. For non-constant coefficient misreads the line "difficulty unchanged" is undefined: of 3240 single +-1 coefficient misreads over the 540 instances, 252 keep distinct integer roots, 468 give rational non-integer roots, 2358 irrational, 108 no real root, 54 no stationary point. Flat branch: 0/1792 keep a repeated root, so only constant misreads can be eligible there (consistent with the generic rule).
findings.evidence: Own enumeration (verify_math.json coefficient_misread_survey). Example: x^3-6x^2+9x+1 with 9x read as 12x gives f'=3(x-2)^2 (two extrema -> one flat point): correctly ineligible, 2/6 vs 5/6 under MR.
findings.repair: E/F: define eligibility (e.g. eligible only if the misread instance stays in the branch's admitted shape class: distinct integer stationary abscissae for two-extrema, a perfect power for flat) and add fixtures.
